correctness.rationale: Decomposing the mean and range into the two nested support-gap indicator pairs yields four elementary covariance terms. Recombination gives the displayed quadratic exactly. The function \(\phi_n(u)\) is strictly decreasing through zero at one half, proving the majority-endpoint sign cases. With both endpoint masses below one half, the transformed expression is a concave quadratic in \(r=t/(1-t)\) with negative root product, hence exactly one positive root and the stated sign change. Independent exact enumeration of bounded rational samples reproduced the formula.

value.rationale: Sample mean and sample range are classical statistics, and zero covariance is a natural weaker dependence question distinct from the well-known independence characterization. The theorem gives the complete support-geometry phase diagram for the smallest nontrivial discrete family, including asymmetric uncorrelated examples and sharp endpoint-mass regimes.
residual_risks: The three-point geometry does not directly extend to higher support sizes.

final_claim: For iid samples from a three-point law with endpoint masses \(a,c\), middle mass \(b\), normalized support \((0,t,1)\), and sample size \(n\ge2\), the covariance of sample mean and sample range is the exact quadratic in RESULT.md; it is positive for all supports when \(a\ge1/2\), negative for all supports when \(c\ge1/2\), and otherwise has exactly one zero support shape given by the displayed radical threshold.
limitations: Three-point finite laws only; covariance sign/uncorrelatedness rather than independence; no four-or-more-point phase diagram.
